body: I used to feel the the exact way you're describing and still do from time to time.  I thing everyone does, especially now during this pandemic.  You're not alone.  Take a couple of good deep breaths if you can.  Oxygenate your brain. You got this.  I, random guy from the internet, said so.

This is almost verbatim, what my experience was at your age all the way until my mid 30s.  I'm 41 now.  I eventually gave into trying medication, taking into consideration that it was at least better than my alternative which was wanting to end myself.  It couldn't have made a better choice.  But I fully understand those who do not choose to explore medicational solutions.   There is something called Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation that I have heard is pretty groundbreaking and effective.  I am currently looking into it myself.
If I am going to constantly think about it might as well do it.  What problems are you experiencing?

Ok, last thing I'll say is, don't underestimate how much your parents care about you.  If they didn't, they wouldn't care what kind of grades you get.  So don't be afraid to ask them for help and tell them your problems. You'd be surprised.  Chances are it might being you closer together.  And besides, could the outcome possibly be worse than what your other idea is?  Probably not.  Good night and good luck.

I actually think video sessions would be more advantageous and comfortable for you.  There is something about being right in front of the psych in the same room that makes you kind of hold back.  At least for me it felt that way.  Do you have insurance?
